Date: 2025-04-02 REMARKS:Examiner Interview Applicant wishes to thank the Examiner for the courtesies extended during the telephonic interview held on April 1, 2025. During the interview, the Examiner and Applicant's representative, Alan Brandt, discussed proposed amendments to independent Claim 50. No agreement was ultimately reached, though considerable progress was made regarding further prosecution.Status of Claims Claim 50 is amended by this paper. Claims 1-4, 6, 8, 12-15, 18, 20, 23-28, 32 and 50 remain pending.Support for Claim Amendments Support for the amendment to Claim 50 may be found, for example, in Paragraph 76 of the specification and Figure 13 of the drawings. No new matter has been added.Allowable Subject Matter The Office action indicates Claims 1-4, 6, 8, 12-15, 18, 20, 23-28 and 32 are allowed.Applicant wishes to thank the Examiner for acknowledging the presence of patentable subject matter.Claim Objection Claim 50 is objected to for a minor informality. The amendment to Claim 50 changes "performing ground operation with for aircraft" to "performing ground operation for the aircraft," thereby obviating the objection.Section 102 Rejection Claim 50 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as allegedly being anticipated by Currey (U.S. Patent No. 3,826,450). The rejection is respectfully traversed.Claim 50, as amended, is drawn to a method for kneeling a landing gear assembly of an aircraft that includes "performing ground operations for the aircraft ...; activating a kneeling feature of the landing gear assembly ...; [and] establishing the kneel stop position in the retract actuator in response to receiving a pressurized fluid from a pressurized fluid source at a kneel stop insert port of the kneel stop assembly.Currey fails to disclose or suggest the combination of features recited in amended Claim 50. In fact, Currey discloses that a "pilot selects differential main landing gear lengths to enable both left and right gears 11 to touch the ground when the airplane 10 is rolled to the number of degrees required to counteract crosswind forces." The differential lengths in Currey are "provided by extending on screw 26 to its maximum stroke and then extending the other screw 26 to whatever length is required to provide the required differential." (Currey, Col. 3, 11. 60-67; see also Fig. 4 (reproduced below).) FIG. 4 38 53 /3~331 r._36 /36.3'3 323 2 4- 1 e 3231 1TO,

26 18 IBZIJIn contrast to Currey, the claimed method defines a technique for establishing a kneel stop position 302 in a retract actuator 104 by inserting a kneel stop segment 1108 of a kneel stop assembly 106 into a kneel stop aperture 1110.Figure 11 of the drawings of the present patent application, which is reproduced below, shows an example of the kneel stop assembly 106, the retract actuator 104, the kneel stop segment 1108, and the kneel stop actuator 1110.FG..1 Currey does not disclose or suggest the claimed arrangement of elements and limitations. Inasmuch as Currey fails to disclose or suggest each and every limitation of Claim 50, as amended, Applicant respectfully submits that Currey cannot, as a matter of law, anticipate Claim 50. Therefore, withdrawal of the rejection of Claim 50 over Currey is respectfully requested.Conclusion For the foregoing reasons, Applicant submits the pending claims of the present application are in condition for allowance. Prompt and favorable action is respectfully requested.The Commissioner is hereby authorized to treat any paper that is filed in this application, which requires an extension of time, as incorporating a request for such an extension. The Commissioner is further authorized to charge any fees required by this paper, or to credit any overpayment, to Deposit Account No. 50-5420.Respectfully submitted, /Victor J.
